body: **2026-11-23-circle-drawer-on-a-canvas** — added `+ decision/circle-drawer-canvas-pixels-only`: Circle Drawer's drawing area is one canvas node, role group, named Drawing area, keyed and clickable, with its circles and diameter labels reaching no DOM, snapshot, accessibility tree, UI graph or lint and leaving only as shot pixels (delegate's choice, PROVISIONAL at the time). This chunk's draw-command read takes those circles and labels out as data for the first time, so it widens the row's "only as shot pixels" clause and must amend it or rule a new crossing; guard `stand_circle_drawer_canvas`.

**2026-11-24T06-11-11-wrap** — `~ decision/circle-drawer-canvas-pixels-only` state provisional → standing: the founder ratified the canvas as one named node with circles and labels leaving only as pixels («Подтвердить (Recommended)», 2026-11-24). The row this chunk widens is now the founder's own word, so changing what leaves the canvas (glyph-run text, coordinates) needs his fork, not a delegate's.

**2026-11-24-upstream-sync-ahead-of-inside-the-canvas** — `+ absence/keyboard-drag-and-drop`: drag and drop reaches a document only as OS pointer drop input, with no keyboard or AT route. This epoch's previous entry; the chunk's boundaries exclude drag, pan and zoom and no canvas keyboard path, so the absence stands unchanged.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (how an open list's labels leave) — new row (now `decision/option-labels-leave-only-as-pixels`): an option's and a group's label leave an open list only as painted pixels in a screenshot and the snapshot's name, with no log site, ratified by the founder as a widening. This is the precedent for authored text leaving the engine as pixels only. A draw-command dump that writes glyph-run text or glyph ids is the same kind of crossing and goes to the founder's fork.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the driver's `type` on any select; the changed set where a list stands) — `type` on any select focuses it with no click and closes any list. This is the origin of `decision/driver-type-focuses-select-no-click`, a change that added nothing to the driver's closed sets of verbs, arguments, key names, result fields, causes, errors or exits. A new verb or argument for the canvas read grows exactly those closed sets, so the row's "adds nothing" precedent and the closed-set enumerations must be checked. The same marker qualified `decision/changed-set-marks` for list open/close.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (the driver on a `multiple` select) — first stated that `type` on a select adds no verb, argument, key name, result field, cause, session error or exit to the driver's closed sets, the wording `decision/driver-type-focuses-select-no-click` keeps. These are the closed sets a new canvas verb or argument enlarges.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — made the driver's `screenshot` one more reader of the model's bounds: an element shot by stable id is its bounds rounded outward and cropped (`contract/driver-screenshot/element-shot`), and a shot changes nothing, with no focus move, `has_changes` false and the next diff empty (`decision/screenshot-changes-nothing`). It also put a password's typed text in no painted frame (`decision/password-never-revealed`). The canvas read sits beside `screenshot` in blitz-test-harness and must meet the same changes-nothing bar. It must also carry no masked text through a scene (a password painted as bullets in blitz-paint).

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** — added the `actions` verb as a read-only reader: it changes nothing (`decision/actions-verb-changes-nothing`), and its answer writes ids, owner ids, verb and cause words and booleans only, never a value, typed text, MASKED_VALUE or NodeId (`contract/actions-answer/fields`, `contract/actions-answer/causes`). It also measured the unpaged Cells answer at 106,088 bytes as a stated limit (residual `res-7cc5bi4k`), and landed the `keyed` field PROVISIONAL (`decision/keyed-wire-form`). This is the nearest precedent for a new read-only driver verb on every carrier: what it may write, its size measured against a budget, and its crossing ruled by the founder.

**2026-11-13T07-43-19-wrap** — `~ decision/keyed-wire-form` provisional → standing on the founder's «Утвердить keyed». A new field on the carriers lands PROVISIONAL under a delegate until the founder's own word. A canvas verb's result fields on the carriers follow the same path.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** — added the read-only UI graph `DioxusDocument::graph` (`decision/ui-graph-carries-no-values`: ids, names, closed words and booleans only, never a value) and reserved the `{owner}///{key}` form (`contract/node-id/reserved-separator`, `virtual_node_id`, which the walk never calls). It built `NodeState.clickable`, so Circle Drawer reads 1 clickable. This chunk must not serve a `///` id: grouping commands by virtual node belongs to «Circle Drawer's circles as virtual nodes». A canvas dump carrying coordinates or text is a values-bearing reader, unlike the graph.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — made the snapshot model consume the accessibility tree with no second role or name mapping (`decision/snapshot-model-single-source`, `decision/readers-of-one-snapshot-model`). A canvas command dump is not a reader of the snapshot model. Its relation to the text form, diff, MCP results, help and screenshot list must be stated, so the "nothing else" readers rule is not breached silently.

**2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization** — made `Snapshot::to_text` a reader of the model, gated by `accessibility`, and masked a file input's value (`contract/snapshot/file-input-value`). A deterministic text form of the snapshot is the precedent for the dump's line form. The masks bind any new dump that could carry painted control text.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — added `Snapshot::diff` as a reader of the model, compared by stable id with a text change reported on its element and never as a text-run entry (`contract/snapshot-diff/entries`). It also made the changed set truthful and the tree refresh on change. This is the precedent for the chunk's "diffable" requirement, where an unchanged step reads an empty diff. The diff's `accessibility` gating is a precedent for where a canvas diff lives.

**2026-10-12-self-description** — added the node keys' help and `DiffNode::differs` (`contract/snapshot-diff/differs`, readings named in node-key order) as model readers with closed words only. It measured a password typed over MCP reading MASKED_VALUE, its sentinel 0 times. The new verb's `help` entry and any changed-lines naming follow this closed-word form, and the sentinel-absence check is the pattern for proving no masked text crosses.

**2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts** — added `Snapshot::text_parts` and paged an over-budget screen by `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` (`contract/snapshot-text/parts`), with an MCP result the text for a whole screen and a JSON line `{text, part, parts}` for a paged one (`contract/mcp-result/snapshot`), on the founder's F1. The chunk must measure the dump's size against this 10,000-byte budget, and a dump that can exceed it raises the same paging question.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — made MCP tool results a reader of the snapshot model, on the crossing the founder ratified (2026-10-10). Whatever the new verb carries over MCP to a model provider is a new crossing and the founder's fork (scope: «authored text in glyph runs»).

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — recorded that the driver's schema defines no role or name set of its own, with `role` and `name` only field names of its result nodes (`decision/driver-schema-has-no-role-set`). A canvas verb's schema and result shape in `schema.rs` / `schema/spec.rs` must not introduce a role or name mapping of its own.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — `escher-driver` names `accessibility` on dioxus-native-dom unconditionally, with no `[features]` table, so the feature reaches every binary depending on it (`decision/driver-requires-accessibility`, `decision/dioxus-accessibility-feature-by-name`). Neither stand binary builds a platform adapter. A canvas verb added to the driver compiles under that feature on every carrier. Any new dependency (e.g. `anyrender_serialize`) must keep the adapter out of the stand graph.

**2026-10-07-driver-session** — first placed `escher-driver` between the stand and the Dioxus bridge with no accessibility feature, deferring the feature to the first snapshot reader. It also ratified the tree's refresh on change and the changed-set contract. This is the history behind `decision/driver-requires-accessibility` and `decision/a11y-tree-refresh-on-change`.

**2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — made every element of a Dioxus document carry its stable id as `author_id` (`contract/accessibility-tree/author-id`). It wired the Dioxus `accessibility` feature by name only and routed the tree through `Document::accessibility_tree`. The canvas read addresses one canvas element by that stable id.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — added the actionable-key rule and `unkeyed_actionable` (`decision/actionable-key-rule`), on the founder's word. The trap is to key an element and never satisfy the check with a `tabindex` or a role. The stand canvas is keyed and clickable, and any stand edit for the read keeps it keyed with the Tab order unmoved.

**2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep** — made `unkeyed_actionable` read 0 on Circle Drawer, its dialog open included. It pinned the click-without-role count (Circle Drawer 1). These are the stand's Circle Drawer a11y readings that the chunk's stand edits must leave unmoved.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** — made a password input read MASKED_VALUE in the snapshot (`contract/snapshot/password-value`, `decision/password-value-masked`). A canvas dump of glyph runs must not become a path by which typed or masked text leaves.

**2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist** — set the obs sink's target allowlist: `text`, `value`, `html` and `attrs` are redacted for `escher_*` targets and an outside target is dropped whole. A canvas verb's logging must write no glyph text or command payload outside this rule, keeping the "no log site" bar of the pixels-only rows.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** — added the second record class (one line per closed span of an admitted target, ratified 2026-10-09). A new driver verb gets a command span whose recorded fields fall under the same allowlist.

**2026-10-07-settle-detection** — a harness settle neither reads nor drains the changed set, and a freshly booted document holds a non-empty set (`decision/harness-settle-leaves-changed-set`, guard `stand_settle`). A changes-nothing check of the canvas read that uses `has_changes` must drain first.

**2026-11-21-engine-debts** — `~ decision/changed-set-marks` to its present rule (post-layout focus loss marks too; node creation, hover, active, other scrolls and layout alone do not). The canvas read runs no step and must mark nothing in this set.

**2026-11-20-select-list-and-selection-debts** — `~ decision/changed-set-marks` (a highlight moving rows marks the set), with the snapshot's highlighted reading added from the tree. This is an earlier step of the row this chunk rests on for its changes-nothing reading.
**2026-11-13-upstream-sync-determinism-and-exploration** — `~ decision/changed-set-marks` (a scroll that closes a list marks its select). This is an earlier step of the picked row.

**2026-11-19-upstream-sync-ahead-of-the-debts** — `~ decision/a11y-tree-refresh-on-change` and `~ decision/accessibility-tree-through-document-method`: the tree is pushed in a redraw after style resolve only when the changed set is non-empty, and a poll pushes no tree. A read that changes nothing triggers no tree push.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** — made blending paint: `render_element` pushes and pops viewport-wide blend layers in blitz-paint, with no frame test (a CARRY on «Upstream sync ahead of determinism and exploration»). `text_contrast` reads None past a blend. The chunk's dump records push/pop layer commands from widget scenes, and this record says what layers paint_scene adds around them that are not the widget's.

**2026-10-25-capability-statement** — `docs/capabilities.md` publishes the accessibility reach under `## Accessibility reach` (tier 0, SC 2.1.1 · 1.4.3 · 2.4.3, AT reading unmeasured; `decision/accessibility-reach-tier-0`), changed by hand. The AT witness is owned by residual `res-llkgqygv` (re-carried). The chunk edits `docs/capabilities.md` for a new verb and must leave the reach section true. A canvas read is no AT route (`absence/assistive-technology-reach` stands).

**2026-11-18-capability-statement** — the capability statement's pin now reads the a11y leg's file count among the section's claims, and no check reads the rest. A README tool count or capability edit for the new verb is pinned by `.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py`, while the reach claims stay hand-held.

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** (the stand's graph re-read) — the stand's graph is re-read at each lock move, with no `accesskit_xplat` / `accesskit_winit`. The adapter and its windowed AT witness are owned by residual `res-llkgqygv`. If the chunk takes `anyrender_serialize` or another crate into the driver or harness, the adapter probe is re-read.

**2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness** — Enter and Space activation build a synthetic Click, and a click focuses a button. This is the source of `decision/synthetic-click-at-node-centre` (a primary click at the node's centre), which the canvas chunks' click synthesis rests on. The scope keeps click synthesis unchanged.

Two levels: a summary (a count per command kind and the canvas's size, or a closed digest of the scene) and a full level (one entry per command in paint order, layers as nesting).
Deterministic and host-independent (same bytes in and across processes and on linux x86_64, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64), and diffable before and after a step, a step that changes nothing reading an empty diff.

body: The new read changes nothing: like the screenshot and the actions verb, it runs no step on the held instance and leaves the document and the engine's changed set as they were.
Circle Drawer's drawing area stays one named canvas node in the accessibility tree and the snapshot; the read reaches its content as data without adding virtual nodes or children to that node.

The canvas is named by its stable element id as the snapshot serves it (the author id and the served node id form); the read's refusal causes for a missing or non-canvas element follow the driver refusal answers.

Glyph runs carry the authored text of the canvas's labels in another form (glyph ids, font data): what crosses to a model provider on each carrier is the founder's fork, met against the rules that redact text and values on the carriers and never reveal password text.

The read's result goes out on the carriers (command line, MCP tool result, recording and replay) in the keyed wire form the other driver results take; the driver schema still defines no role or name set.
The read's diff before and after a step names exactly what changed and reads empty when nothing changed, alongside the snapshot diff's entries and differs.
The read is a reader beside the snapshot readers: whether it stands behind the accessibility feature as the snapshot readers do, while the session library always enables accessibility.
Capability statement and README tool count edited by hand where a verb is added, with accessibility reach left as stated (tier 0).
Size measured against the snapshot's 10,000-byte budget at boot and after circles are added, at each level.

Determinism across the three CI hosts: glyph positions from shaping may differ by host (the macOS glyph-origin snap the canvas element shot's cross-OS digest watches), so numbers are written at a stated rounding and measured, not assumed.
The canvas's existing paint path, placement, pointer frame, font hand-off and click synthesis at the node's centre stay as built; the scene is read without a raster.
The canvas element shot of the driver's screenshot keeps its digest equal across the three hosts (the folded watch).

body: Keyboard navigation: no canvas keyboard path, no Tab order, focus, activation or arrow-key behaviour is added or changed.
Select lists, list boxes, range inputs, the Cells grid and the CRUD list: no control of these kinds is touched.
Contrast and the visual lint: no canvas lint and no contrast measure is built (the next entry builds the canvas lint).
ARIA role mapping, ARIA states and property reads, accessible-name precedence and hidden-content exclusion: no role, state, name or hidden rule changes.
Cognitive accessibility: no invalid-state signalling or timeout is touched.
Drag and drop, pan and zoom: no drag, pan or zoom is added.

**2026-11-23-canvas-in-a-headless-shot** (Established Decisions: 2 rows) — added `decision/canvas-crosses-as-pixels`: a canvas's app-painted content crosses the driver's carriers only as pixels in a screenshot, with no new carrier, verb, field, exit, cause, session error, log field or span, ratified by the founder («Ратифицировать для всех каналов»). It also added `decision/harness-paints-custom-widgets`, which names blitz-paint's custom-widget feature in blitz-test-harness. Why it matters: a draw-command verb carries canvas content as data, so it directly reverses this decision. The decision has to be amended or replaced as a boundary widening on the founder's own word, which is the carrier fork the scope names. The harness's feature edge is what makes a widget's `Scene` reachable from a harness read beside `screenshot`.

**2026-11-23-canvas-placement-and-text** (Established Decisions and Standard Contracts) — added `decision/custom-widget-content-box-paint`, now ratified: the paint size is the content box times the scale, floored at 0, and the scene is appended at the content origin inside the element's transform, unclipped, guarded by `stand_canvas_placement`. It also added `contract/nodes-widgets/widget-fonts` (`Widget::fonts` gets the document's shared Parley font context before each paint) and `contract/base-document/font-ctx`. Why it matters: the dump's coordinates and the canvas size it reports come from this placement rule. A glyph run's font data comes from the document's shared font context, which bears on the premise about referencing fonts by digest or index and on the authored-text fork.

**2026-11-23-canvas-shot-across-hosts** (Existing Scopes and Occupied Resources) — gave `decision/no-screenshot-in-cross-os-byte-check` a canvas-only exception: one committed digest table holds a canvas-only shot byte-equal on linux x86_64, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64, while a shot holding document text stays out. It also restated `decision/committed-stand-checks`' reason as "a shot holding document text differs by OS". This rests on the founder's F1 «A: требовать побайтовое равенство». Why it matters: it is the precedent and the measured base for the chunk's claim of a hardware-independent dump across the three CI hosts. The same text-versus-canvas split is the premise to measure for glyph positions (the WATCH on `stand_canvas_cross_os`).

**2026-11-23-circle-drawer-on-a-canvas** (Established Decisions: 3 rows) — added `decision/widget-click-synthesis` and `decision/widget-click-point-content-box` (read a click point against the content box, not the client rect). It also added to `decision/click-focuses-button` the exception that a custom-widget click runs no click walk. Why it matters: these rules shape the steps whose before/after dumps must diff, for example adding circles on the stand's one canvas. The boundaries say click synthesis stands as built.

**2026-11-23-circle-drawer-on-a-canvas** (Standard Contracts: 2 rows) — changed `contract/headless-stand/boot` to add Circle Drawer's boot, which runs in process only and is served by no escher-session role («A: не сейчас»). It also added `decision/canvas-placement-at-click-centre`. Why it matters: this is the premise that a verb on the command line, MCP or a kept check reaches no stand canvas until Circle Drawer is served or a fixture serves one. The carrier fork depends on it. The size measurement of Circle Drawer's canvas also runs on this in-process boot.

**2026-11-24T06-11-11-wrap** — `decision/canvas-placement-at-click-centre` went from provisional to standing on the founder's «Подтвердить». Why it matters: the picked row is now ratified, and it is a measured limit stated in the tool's help. A canvas verb's help and the capability statement must keep it consistent.

**2026-11-24-upstream-sync-ahead-of-inside-the-canvas** — the last sync before this chunk:
- `decision/taffy-layout` now reads Taffy 0.16 from crates.io, and the Taffy exception was dropped from `decision/no-git-dependencies`.
- The rule in `decision/one-axis-clip-readings-kept` now covers paint as well.
- Added `contract/nodes-widgets/widget-drop-acceptance` and the OS drop input, both PROVISIONAL.
- `decision/default-action-event-order` gained a clause.

Why it matters: the `Widget` trait this chunk reads (`paint -> Scene`) changed again with drop acceptance, which is still provisional, and the merge surface of blitz-paint's widget paint path moved. No git dependency may come back with a new crate.

**2026-11-17-upstream-sync-ahead-of-polish-and-ship** (Stack and Technologies) — changed `decision/anyrender-rendering-abstraction` to the AnyRender 0.15 set, where vello-gpu replaced vello-hybrid. Two skrifa versions now stand (0.44 with parley, 0.49 with the renderers), under `decision/skrifa-matches-parley`. Why it matters: the widget `Scene`, its `RenderCommand`s and `GlyphRunCommand` are AnyRender 0.15 types, and the `anyrender_serialize` option belongs to this set. A glyph run's font, resolved through skrifa, sits on this version split.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** (the `screenshot` verb, `fonts-unavailable`, `Outcome::Shot` and the MCP image block) — added the eleventh verb. It takes one optional `id`, dispatches nothing, is no step and changes nothing. A `fonts-unavailable` refusal is checked before anything is painted, and the shot's line, its base64 and the MCP image block are hand-written with no base64 crate. Why it matters: this is the closest precedent for a no-step canvas read named by id: how it resolves an id, refuses `off-screen` and `fonts-unavailable`, writes its answer by hand, and records only `verb` on the `command` span.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** (the harness's screenshot and the image in band) — added `Harness::screenshot` and `screenshot_rect`, which paint through blitz-paint into `VelloCpuImageRenderer` and composite over white. This gave the harness its `blitz-paint`, `anyrender` and `anyrender_vello_cpu` dependencies. The image in band was ratified as the founder's fork 1. Why it matters: the scope wants "a read of one canvas's scene, beside `screenshot`" in `packages/blitz-test-harness/src/`. The harness already reaches blitz-paint and anyrender here, and the screenshot's `FontsUnavailable` and `EmptyRect` errors are the pattern a scene read would follow.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the UI graph crosses the ratified carriers, and the `graph` verb) — added the thirteenth verb as a ratified widening. The changes ran through `VERBS`, `FieldKind`, `describe()` counts, `Command` and `Outcome`, the hand-written answer form, `tools/list`, kept-check verbs, the README tool count and the cold-agent tool list. The `command` span records `verb` alone. Why it matters: it lists every site a new verb must touch, and it records a new content class crossing the carriers only on the founder's own word.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (fourteen verbs, and the actions read with its shared per-verb target check) — added `actions`. `contract/actions-verb/target-verbs` covers each instance verb that takes an id argument, and `check_target` is the single per-verb target check shared by every id-taking arm. Why it matters: trap — if the canvas read takes an `id`, the actions answer and its acceptance check automatically list it for every node. The read must go through the shared `check_target`, and its no-cause or cause behaviour must be stated, as `layout` was.

**2026-11-16-layout-explained** — added `contract/driver-session/layout` as an in-process read that opens no span, and narrowed `decision/driver-spans-only` to "per call its run path runs, an in-process read outside the run path opening none". It also landed `decision/layout-read-in-process-only` as PROVISIONAL, on the delegate's answer, while the founder's carrier word was owed. Why it matters: it is the precedent for building a read in process first and leaving its carrier crossing to the founder's fork. It also states the span rule a canvas read must meet in either form.

**2026-11-17-layout-on-the-carriers** (Standard Contracts, all four parts) — added the fifteenth verb `layout`. It changed `contract/verb-table/order`, `driver-session/command-schema`, `mcp-server/tools-list`, `kept-check/kept-verbs` and `kept-check-reader/strict-read` (eleven instance verbs), and `actions-verb/target-verbs` (`layout` fifth, with no cause). `driver-explore/explored-verbs` now leaves out a verb whose result holds an image or a layout-reading field kind. `decision/layout-read-in-process-only` was replaced by `decision/layout-answer-crossing`, and closed-word answer-JSON rows with fallback words were added. Why it matters: it is the most recent full template for a sixteenth verb, including its order, every count site, the explore rule that selects by field kind (a draw-command field kind needs a decision there), and closed-set fallback words for non-exhaustive engine enums such as `RenderCommand`.

**2026-11-17-layout-on-the-carriers** (Established Decisions: 2 rows) — widened the closed list in `decision/no-node-id-across-session` to "… layout readings, closed words, booleans, counts and numbers". It also widened `decision/select-list-crossing`'s "only as pixels" to admit the layout placing words. Why it matters: a draw-command dump adds a new class to the closed list of what crosses a session, so that list must name it. The select-list precedent shows that an "only as pixels" crossing is narrowed by an explicit, ratified amendment and never silently.

**2026-11-17-a-component-in-isolation** — added `absence/component-alone-on-carriers` and put the one-component boot in `contract/headless-stand/boot`. Its delegate-confirmed cards were then ratified. Why it matters: like a fixture state, a stand surface reached in process only is recorded as a stated absence on the carriers. If the canvas verb stays in process or Circle Drawer stays unserved, the same absence form applies.

**2026-11-14-start-in-a-state** — added `absence/fixture-state-on-carriers`, `contract/headless-stand/start-in` and `contract/driver-session/reach`. Why it matters: the scope's premise says a canvas reaches a carrier only once it is served "or a fixture serves one". This row says a fixture state is on no carrier, so a fixture route needs its own ratified widening.

**2026-11-18-served-error-page** (Standard Contracts, both parts) — moved the served-task set from six to seven, adding `order`. The changes reached `decision/stand-readings-same-on-every-ci-os`, `contract/escher-session-cli/usage`, `escher-session/invocation`, `escher-session/mcp`, `headless-stand/boot` and the cold-agent pass bar. It measures the dump's size for Circle Drawer's canvas at each level, at boot and after circles are added, against the snapshot's 10,000-byte budget; it adds no canvas lint, no virtual nodes, no new painting.

A glyph run carries glyph ids and font data, not text; a dump that writes a label as text, or as glyph ids, still carries authored page text, so where that text may leave (which ratified exits, whether it may reach a model provider) is the founder's fork and must be stated against the rules for attribute text and accessible names.
Font data and image data in a draw command cross only by reference (a digest or an index), never inline: no font bytes or image bytes in the answer.
The read changes nothing and runs nothing: no step, no settle, no move of session state, no clock read — like the actions read — and two reads of one state answer the same bytes.

The new verb or argument joins the closed driver verb schema and passes the single validation gate shared by every carrier (command line, session socket, MCP); its arguments use the existing closed argument kinds.

The canvas is named by its stable element id, looked up anew on each call; an unknown id is refused as stale or not-found, a non-canvas or unfit element is refused by the shared target check in the fixed refusal order; no NodeId or other process-local handle crosses in the answer.
A refusal of the new verb uses the closed refusal cause set with its fixed texts and holds nothing the call supplied.

The answer stays inside the existing bounds: the driver command line's answer bounds, the session socket's oversize reply and the MCP tool result's size bound; the full level's size at boot and after circles are added is measured against the snapshot's 10,000-byte budget, and whether the full level is paged or bounded is decided against those measures.

Determinism across hosts: numbers written at a stated rounding, no host-dependent value (glyph positions from shaping may differ by host and are measured, not assumed); the Circle Drawer canvas shot's SAMPLE digest held equal on the three CI hosts in stand_canvas_cross_os is kept.
The read takes the widget's recorded scene without a raster and changes no painting: the paint path, the shot pixels and the custom widget's frame stand as built.
Diffability: a before/after comparison names the dump lines added, removed or changed; any log of a diff carries its sizes only, never its lines.

No dump content (labels, glyph ids, coordinates, commands) is logged: the command span and the MCP tool_call span stay content-free with the verb name and cause only, and escher targets withhold content-named fields.

If the verb is recorded into a kept check, the recorded check file gains the canvas answer: kept whole, owner-only and uncommitted, read back strictly as untrusted bytes and replayed through the session; whether the canvas answer may enter a kept check at all is part of the carrier fork.
The MCP tool for the read: the tool listing and help stay fixed program text, the tool's arguments use the closed MCP value kinds, and its result follows the tool result shape and isError rule.
The committed capability statement and the README's tool count state the new verb or tool, and the capability statement check holds them equal to the driver's verbs.

Circle Drawer is not served by escher-session: a command-line, MCP or kept-check carrier reaches no stand canvas until it is served or a fixture serves one; a fixture state name added for it joins the closed fixture table.
A cold-agent run carries the screen to the model provider; whether the canvas dump may join what reaches the provider is the founder's fork, and the model's reply stays untrusted input.

If the dump reuses anyrender's serialize feature or anyrender_serialize, it is taken at the workspace-inherited version under locked builds, the licence gate and the dependency audit; the test harness keeps taking no tracing and no style and keeps blitz-paint's custom-widget feature on.

Untrusted input: hostile or huge page content under a canvas (NaN or infinite floats, deep layer nesting, many commands) is written without panic and inside the bounds; caller input is never echoed in the answer.
Evidence written for the founder's forks holds no raw log with a temp or home path and no credential; live evidence follows the operator's-own-login rule.

The read answers at two levels, a summary (a count per command kind and the canvas's size, or a closed digest) and a full level (one entry per command in paint order, layers as nesting), deterministic across processes and the three CI hosts, and diffable before and after a step.
A driver verb carries it (a sixteenth verb of the verb table or an argument of an existing one), on the carriers the founder rules; what may cross to a model provider is the founder's fork.
It measures the dump's size for Circle Drawer's canvas on the stand at each level, at boot and after circles are added, against the snapshot's 10,000-byte budget.
It adds no new painting, no canvas lint and no virtual nodes; Dioxus stays at 0.7.3.

body: The canvas read: one canvas element by its stable element id, on the held instance, answering the eight draw command kinds its widget recorded; it runs no step, settles nothing and changes nothing of the instance.

The two levels of the answer: a summary (a count per command kind and the canvas's size, or a closed digest of the scene) and a full level (one line or object per command in paint order, layers as nesting).

Determinism: two reads of one state answer the same bytes in process and across processes, and on the linux x86_64, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64 CI hosts; numbers are written at a stated rounding; the cross-host comparison is a byte or digest comparison holding no shot.

Diffability: a read before and after a step names exactly the lines added, removed or changed, and a step that changes nothing reads an empty diff; the no-change control must carry pending work to be a control.
Size measured: the dump of Circle Drawer's canvas on the stand, at each level, at boot and after circles are added, stated in bytes against the snapshot's 10,000-byte text budget.

The driver verb: a sixteenth verb in the verb table or an argument of an existing verb, with its lookup, level check, result shape, JSON writer, help text, MCP tool in the tools list and its order, and its place in a recorded kept check and its replay.

The carriers of the read (the session command line, the MCP role, a recording) are the founder's fork; Circle Drawer is not yet served by the session binary, so a carrier reaches the stand canvas only once it is served or a fixture serves one.

What crosses: a glyph run carries glyph ids and font data, not text, and a dump of either still carries authored text in some form; what the read may carry to a model provider is the founder's fork, so the session's rules that it writes and logs nothing of the screen and returns no typed value bind the answer and its log lines.
Font data and image data in a command cross only by reference (a digest or an index), never inline, so the answer stays host-independent and within the size budget.

The widget's recorded scene is read without a raster: the painter builds widget scenes during the paint and drops them after, so the read needs the recorded scene with no screenshot taken and no font-unavailable refusal from a raster it never makes.
The harness read of one canvas's scene stands beside the harness screenshot, on a harness-built instance; it is held to the harness contract's construction and inspection helpers.

Refusals of the read: an id that names no element or a stale one, a malformed argument, and an element that is no canvas each refuse with a cause from the fixed cause set in its order, change nothing and echo no input.

Glyph positions from text shaping may differ by host (the macOS glyph-origin snap); the read's cross-host sameness is measured, not assumed, and the canvas label's glyph origins on whole device pixels are what the cross-OS canvas shot check already watches.

The capability statement and the README's tool count are held to the driver schema: a new verb adds its claim, names its checks and moves the count and claim section names that the capability check reads.

The stand's boot of Circle Drawer and its shared stand tables are what the read's checks drive, adding circles by the stand's existing click path; the widget paint path, placement, pointer frame, font hand-off and click synthesis stand unchanged.
Evidence of the chunk's forks holds no raw log with a temporary or home path, and a probe worktree stands outside the build directory and is not deleted by a plan step.
